standard.title: Evaluate exhibits and curate exhibitions
standard.description: evaluate art exhibits to inform the curation and exhibition of their own and/or others' artworks and/or visual arts practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can prepare artworks for formal display, create exhibition materials and make deliberate presentation decisions for different audiences (AC9AVA8P01, implied from progression). They have produced artist statements and curated class exhibitions. They have not yet evaluated existing exhibitions as a research base for their own curatorial decisions, or planned exhibitions that communicate a broader curatorial argument.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate art exhibitions to inform the curation and exhibition of their own and/or others' artworks and visual arts practice.

nodes.label: Evaluating exhibitions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can visit or investigate exhibitions (physical or virtual) and evaluate the curatorial and presentational choices made — analysing how these choices create meaning and communicate artists' intentions.
nodes.minimum_width: Visit or investigate one exhibition; identify at least two curatorial choices (spatial arrangement, sequencing, labelling, lighting, grouping) and explain how each serves the exhibition's purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Visit and evaluate exhibitions in physical or virtual galleries, museums or community sites; analyse how artists and curators work together; investigate how curatorial choices create visual narrative and communicate intention; produce written, oral or multimedia evaluations.
wider: Create a virtual or scale model of an exhibition of a researched artist — use this to communicate your understanding of the artist's intentions and refine based on peer feedback
Evaluate an exhibition of contemporary First Nations Australian art — analyse how the curatorial choices reflect Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights and community protocols
nodes.hinge_reason: Exhibition evaluation is the research base for the student's own curation — students who evaluate superficially cannot derive curatorial principles to apply to their own work. The depth of evaluation determines the quality of the curatorial reasoning that follows.

response_modes.reason: Curatorial analysis requires a systematic framework — students need to analyse spatial arrangement, sequencing, labelling and audience flow as deliberate choices, not just notice what they see. Structured evaluation tools build this analytical capacity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two curatorial choices in an exhibition
Explains how each choice serves the exhibition's purpose or communicates the artist's/curator's intentions

nodes.label: Planning and curating exhibitions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and curate an exhibition of their own or others' work — making deliberate decisions about selection, arrangement, sequence and spatial narrative.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a class exhibition: make deliberate decisions about which works to include, how to sequence them and one spatial arrangement choice; explain the reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and curate exhibitions of own work and/or others' works; make deliberate decisions about selection, arrangement and spatial narrative; consider Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights where relevant; develop a coherent curatorial argument.
wider: Plan and curate a community installation or an imagined exhibition of artworks by researched artists — develop and present the curatorial argument in written or multimedia form
Plan an exhibition that explicitly engages with Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights — research the relevant considerations and document how they shaped curatorial decisions

response_modes.reason: Students who curate only a single class exhibition have limited experience of how curatorial decisions change across different contexts (community installation, imagined artist retrospective, physically constrained space). A range of curatorial contexts builds genuine curatorial capability.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Community installation planning, imagined retrospective curation, and exhibitions engaging with ICIP are each qualitatively different curatorial tasks — students who engage with multiple types develop substantially richer curatorial understanding.
success_criteria: Plans an exhibition with deliberate decisions about selection, arrangement and sequence
Articulates at least one curatorial argument — what the exhibition communicates and why specific choices serve it

nodes.label: Exhibition materials and curatorial voice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop exhibition materials — didactic panels, artist statements, branding, press statements — that communicate the curatorial argument and serve the audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least two exhibition materials (e.g. a curatorial statement and an artist label) that communicate the curatorial argument.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a comprehensive set of exhibition materials — didactic panels, artist or curatorial statements, advertising, branding and press statements; evaluate their effectiveness for the intended audience; construct explanations of how artists communicate ideas and meaning.
wider: Develop a full exhibition materials set for a class show — labels, introduction, advertising, press statement and review — and evaluate each element's effectiveness with peer feedback
Create a written, oral or multimedia response to an exhibition of work — connect the curatorial evaluation to the student's own approach in a planned or realised exhibition

response_modes.reason: Exhibition evaluation, curatorial planning and materials development come together in a complete exhibition practice — where the materials serve the curatorial argument and both reflect the student's understanding of how artworks communicate to audiences.

success_criteria: Develops at least two exhibition materials that communicate the curatorial argument
The materials are tailored to the intended audience and context — not generic labels
